evidence: Workbook row 20 (both sheets): reference must be a committed static baseline, not regenerated/fetched/nondeterministic on any pinned value; skill quality-checks.md:87-88 adds: seeding produces the same rows every run, no random ids, no wall-clock-derived values, no boot-time fetch that could move a graded figure, fixed clock is the only time source graded rules use. (1) Committed static baseline: solution/app/** is plain committed source (package.json, server.js, src/{bootstrap,db,index}.js, src/seed_data.json, public/**); no build step, no generator, no lockfile-less npm install in solve.sh. solve.sh only checks DB inactivity, does `cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/` and deletes the disposable app.db/-wal/-shm, so every install starts from the same committed bytes (stricter than template solve.sh, which only copies). Dependencies are pinned exact (package.json: better-sqlite3 12.4.1, express 5.1.0) and pre-installed in environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile at those exact versions; test.sh runs node with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules and performs no install. (2) Seed determinism: src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (sha256 a1c65c80...7740, cmp identical) and is read from beside the module (db.js:10), not from /assets or the network. seedIfEmpty (db.js) inserts users/jobs/applications/messages/reads/notes in file order with fixed values: application created_at is the literal '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z', message/note created_at come from the seed (2026-07-01..2026-07-29 literals), message ids are AUTOINCREMENT in array order, read markers resolve via read_count to those deterministic ids, seeded IDs (APP-101, USR-REC1...) come from the file. No 'now'/random/template placeholder in the seed. Seeding happens once (skipped when users exist). (3) Randomness/wall clock: index.js:59 now() = new Date().toISOString() and index.js:60 uid() = crypto.randomBytes(3) are used only for rows created at runtime (sessions token, new job/application ids, activity/actions/notes/messages created_at). The brief pins neither: hireops_rules.md:38 'Identifiers are generated by the workspace', and the task has no fixed clock (grep of instruction.md, rules, integration.md, app_context.md and judge.toml finds no fixed date/clock or time-derived graded figure). Graded orderings use ids/positions, not timestamps: Activity ORDER BY a.id DESC (index.js:189), threads ORDER BY id (407-412), board ORDER BY position, id (199), undo by latest action id (350); stale-move refusal is version-based (index.js:240-244), not time-window based. Candidate list orders by created_at,id (173), where seeded rows are a fixed 2026-06-15 and new rows are later wall-clock, so the order is stable. The only time-window rule (live updates within 15 s, hireops_rules.md:117) is product behaviour, not a pinned value. Frontend js (app.js/board.js/threads.js) has no Math.random; dates are only formatted (app.js:21, UTC). (4) No boot-time fetch: no external http(s) URLs in solution/app js/html/css; bootstrap.js only proxies to the local worker. Run evidence: raw-evidence-index hashes re-verified (all 6 artifacts and every matching_source_files hash equal the frozen bytes); workspace.json result 'seeded card order and internal notes are loaded' passed with page_errors [] in a scripted golden run (not a judge/Oracle run). Counterexample search: a broken reference that seeded created_at with Date.now(), generated seed ids randomly, or fetched seed from /assets/network at boot would fail this row; none of these occur. A conforming alternative app using random ids or wall-clock timestamps for new records is not penalised because no criterion pins runtime ids/times. Notes (non-blocking, P3 latent): uid() uses 3 random bytes with no collision retry, so a PK collision on a new job/application would surface as a server error (probability ~1e-4 per review at tens of inserts); Docker image build resolves express/better-sqlite3 transitive dependency ranges at build time (top-level pinned), which is environment build-time fetching allowed under the public-network profile, not regeneration of the reference.
run_verdict_note: Static source inspection establishes determinism; one scripted golden run (hash-verified, not a judge run) confirmed seeded order loads. Repeated fresh seeding was not separately executed in this review; not required to decide this row.
